A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WeightLens/CircuitLens research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original feature-description evaluations, token-validation results across three models, circuit case studies and analyses of clustering and downstream influence.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations across additional Gemma layers, revised metric scores, new validation and clustering case studies, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The weight-projection, token-validation, attribution and description-generation pipelines are retained. However, v1 Section 3.2 and v2 Section 3.3 specify DBSCAN, while v2 Appendix E.5 specifies HDBSCAN. This inconsistency prevents determining whether the clustering algorithm actually changed.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Pile-uncopyrighted and the same feature-interpretation tasks involving GPT-2 Small, Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.2-1B transcoders. Additional layers and illustrative features extend evaluation within this coverage rather than introduce new datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Neuronpedia and MaxAct* remain the quantitative baselines, with the same proposed-method variants. Appendix E.1 and Figure 11 newly compare WeightLens graphs with Circuit Tracer's input-dependent graphs, adding a limited qualitative comparator.

E3.justification: Reported FADE evaluation expands from four Gemma layers to ten, extending sampling across network depth. Appendix B revises the large corpus from 3.6B to 2.3B tokens while retaining its stated 6GB size. Figure 17 also introduces an eps=0.7 versus 0.8 clustering comparison. These are reported setting changes and additions, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained circuit examples and downstream-influence analyses, Appendix E adds weight-versus-circuit comparisons, token-validation false negatives, spurious-connection examples, polysemantic feature analysis and clustering sensitivity. These substantially extend evidence about the methods' mechanisms and failure modes.

E5.justification: Both versions report aggregate scores and feature-score distributions through density plots and histograms. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; the additional result panels retain the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Shared-layer scores change substantially: WeightLens layer-0 Clarity/Responsiveness/Purity change from 0.56/0.24/0.03 in v1 Table 1 to 0.67/0.72/0.50 in v2 Table 2. CircuitLens scores also change, and six additional layers, case-study findings and runtime results are reported. These are revised or added results, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(5), the outlier and token-activation assumptions, inverse-frequency sampling, frequency filtering and Jaccard construction retain their mathematical substance. Revised assumption wording and expanded FADE explanations do not introduce a substantive derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central contributions: weight-based interpretation of context-independent features and circuit-based interpretation of contextual and polysemantic behavior. Expanded evidence and clarified wording about explainer dependence do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit architectural applicability limits and acknowledges CircuitLens's continuing dataset and explainer dependence. Appendix E substantially extends interpretation through direct versus upstream-mediated activation, validation false negatives, propagation of noisy descriptions and clustering overfragmentation, beyond v1's more general caveats.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies model-specific outlier thresholds, baseline sampling details, FADE computation explanations, clustering parameters, sparse-cache requirements and A100 runtime accounting. Appendix E.3 also states that precomputed feature analyses are available in the existing repository. These materially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing that previously unspecified settings changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hanna et al. (2025) for Circuit Tracer while retaining the other cited works. It also more explicitly credits output-centric projection methods and contrasts embedding-only interpretation with upstream-feature analysis in Appendix E.1; the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The methodology is substantially reorganized into shared attribution foundations followed by complete WeightLens and CircuitLens pipelines, with sampling moved before pattern detection. Results narratives are extensively rewritten, and dedicated limitations, computational-cost, baseline and case-study sections expand the structure. Existing prompts are retained in the renumbered appendix.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the WeightLens schematic with a three-step illustration, presents main comparisons as bar charts, and redesigns numerical tables in Appendix G. The token/context comparison becomes a line plot, while a runtime table, seven case-study figures and expanded density panels substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: New failure and sensitivity cases, implementation thresholds and runtime accounting make v2's applicability and practical use clearer, while broader layer evaluation strengthens its empirical account. These support a net improvement over v1. However, unexplained large revisions to shared-layer scores and the conflicting DBSCAN/HDBSCAN descriptions limit confidence in a larger quality improvement.
